revision: Workbench HEAD 0534135d877ec3679bb91ee0b4a68b71e174ff7a plus the existing dirty WB-01..WB-19 tree and the tested WB-20 changes; no commit or push was made. WB-20 code, tests, UI-grid output and performance artifacts are identified below.
environment: macOS 26.4.1 arm64, Macmini9,1; Neovim 0.11.7 minimum and 0.12.4 current/host; Git 2.54.0; Python 3.14.6; mini.test 0.16.0; pynvim 0.6.0; msgpack 1.1.1. Linux was unavailable locally.
summary: Added a bounded asynchronous read-only Git provider that parses porcelain-v2 NUL records structurally, retains rename source paths, coalesces refreshes, caches repository snapshots, aggregates status, identifies linked worktrees/submodules, and limits selected-file diff previews. Added a Git status controller/action with explicit diff and refresh keys; cursor movement performs no Git work. Git-missing and non-Git states are visible. Cancellation, delayed exits and disposal release owned processes, views and callbacks. A shared list-view viewport calculation was corrected after the RPC grid exposed a selection/scroll defect that otherwise made diff lines unreachable. No staging, discard, commit or conflict-resolution operation is exposed.

gates.command: make check-ownership; inspect docs/tasks.json#WB-20 ownership and the final diff for allowed-path/dependency review
gates.result: Ownership checks passed for 35 Workbench Lua modules. WB-20 changes stay within its claimed provider, controller, shared view, tests, Makefile and evidence paths. The provider owns process/cache lifetimes and has no UI dependency; the controller owns per-tab views/actions and delegates status/diff work; the shared view owns selection/scroll rendering. Only the Workbench repository changed. The UI view path was added to the task claim after a reproducible actual-grid defect demonstrated the needed shared fix.

All 131 mini.test cases passed on Neovim 0.11.7 and 0.12.4. Git tests cover porcelain ordinary/rename/unmerged/untracked records, spaces/newlines, real staged rename and untracked diffs, cache hits, same-root refresh coalescing, non-Git roots, linked worktrees, submodules, large-output truncation, and rejection of forged paths. Controller coverage verifies explicit diff, process-free cursor movement, missing-Git visibility, and view behavior.

gates.command: make test; inspect cancellation, coalescing, cache and consumer-disposal cases in tests/runtime/test_git_provider.lua and tests/runtime/test_git_controller.lua
gates.result: Two rapid refresh consumers share one identity/status process chain and receive their own generations; a subsequent cached refresh launches no process. Closing the status consumer while identity is pending kills the owned process, clears provider/controller/layout requests, and ignores a late stdout/exit callback. Closing a completed diff restores focus to Git status and closing all views leaves zero active requests/windows. No sibling action or editor-owned buffer is removed.

The real RPC/ext_linegrid journey passed on both Neovim versions at all four grids: open a repository's Git status, move with j, explicitly preview the selected untracked file with d, navigate into the bounded diff to see +new content, close the diff back to status, then close status back to the editor. The grid confirmed 0 processes for cursor movement and exactly 1 for the selected diff. Repository status remained unchanged; editor cwd/buffer and focus were preserved. Result/screen artifacts are retained in the listed run directories.

gates.command: .test-deps/venv/bin/python bench/startup.py --runs 5 --nvim nvim; inspect WB-20 real-grid result.json timings and the fresh /tmp/wb20-startup-final-20260913.log profile
gates.result: Host startup marker was 45.147 ms p50 / 50.366 ms p95 across five interleaved samples, below the 150 ms budget and consistent with the previous WB-19 46.636 ms single-run marker. First RPC frame was 58.260/59.916 ms p50/p95 and first-input state 1.829/1.950 ms. No Git provider/controller/view module was loaded in the startup profile. First selected-diff latency across minimum/current Neovim and the four grids was 17.069–23.257 ms; one repository identity/status chain used 2 processes, cursor motion 0, and explicit diff 1. A single fresh marker was a 72.564 ms outlier but remained under budget; the repeated distribution showed no WB-20 startup regression.
